quarterly_data.signal: 2025 annual report: revenue RMB 96,748,339,344.03, up 22.43%; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 1,685,521,754.82 (+7.19%), excluding non-recurring items RMB 1,634,660,607.17 (+12.26%); gross margin 14.59% (down 2.80 points). ICT infrastructure and services revenue RMB 76,846,762,924.64 (+41.11%), 79.43% of revenue, gross margin 16.51%; IT product distribution and supply-chain services RMB 25,561,918,394.39 (-12.72%), gross margin 5.20%. Overseas revenue RMB 4,710,527,747.84 (+53.59%, gross margin 23.55%); direct sales RMB 48,566,509,801.63 (+52.28%). Quarterly revenue: Q1 RMB 20,789,771,379.75, Q2 RMB 26,635,007,699.70, Q3 RMB 29,896,726,323.53, Q4 RMB 19,426,833,941.05. Operating cash flow RMB 3,486,751,492.84 (+42.86%).

H3C (2025 annual report): subsidiary New H3C's 2025 revenue was RMB 759.81 hundred million, up 37.96%, and net profit RMB 31.51 hundred million, up 12.30%. Its domestic government and enterprise revenue reached RMB 658.46 hundred million (+48.84%) as it targeted core links of AI build-out, and its international revenue RMB 46.20 hundred million (+58.45%). Overseas partners number nearly 3,800 across more than 180 countries and regions, with 22 overseas subsidiaries.

quarterly_data.signal: AI networking and scale-up (2025 annual report): its 51.2T CPO silicon-photonics data center switch completed interoperability verification with several suppliers' 800G optical modules and test instruments in 2025, passed POC tests at several strategic customers and reached batch delivery and deployment. Its scale-up whole-rack work is progressing: a 32-card switch node built on a leading domestic GPU maker's solution is ready for POC demonstration and small-batch shipment, and 64-card / 256-card switch nodes are in board bring-up with ports lit. Its 200G/400G/800G switches with domestic key chips have shipped at scale in government, power-energy and enterprise sectors, and a higher-performance 51.2T domestic-chip intelligent-computing switch is in development. Its DDC lossless-network architecture reached scaled deployment in 2025 across government, enterprise and internet customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 51.2T CPO switch in batch delivery; 32-card scale-up switch node ready for small-batch shipment

quarterly_data.signal: Customers and wins (2025 annual report): it has built 48 mid-to-large intelligent computing centers with telecom operators and 8 'Turing Town' compute operation projects with local governments; it continues building large compute clusters and supernode systems with several leading internet customers, joining their next-generation AI infrastructure build-out. Its servers, switches, routers and security products won procurement tenders at China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and China Tower, and it completed with China Mobile what it calls the industry's first live-network trial of 800G Ethernet intelligent-computing collaborative training. It serves more than 4,000 Chinese financial institutions and over 90% of power-energy companies.
quarterly_data.figure: 48 intelligent computing centers built with operators; 8 Turing Towns

quarterly_data.signal: R&D and products (2025 annual report): R&D investment RMB 4,952,674,806.36 (-2.92%), 5.12% of revenue; 6,159 R&D staff. Releases completed in 2025 include the new flagship R5500 AI server (supports trillion-parameter model training and migration of 15+ mainstream open-source models), new R4700 / 4900 general servers on the latest Intel processors, the DDC2 data center switch (400G/800G interfaces, non-blocking cell switching), the S9855-32DH-G box switch with 32 400GE ports and a 36-port 400G line card for the S125CR chassis on domestic chips, the Polaris X20000 distributed storage upgrade (100% performance gain) and the UniPoD S80000 supernode with liquid-cooled key components; it also launched cold-plate, immersion and phase-change liquid-cooled servers and switches and high-density liquid-cooled racks.

Construction in progress RMB 573,184,168.51 at end-2025 (RMB 239,607,050.20 a year earlier), mainly the Unisplendour Digital Economy Science Park phase 1 smart-factory project (budget RMB 448,134,197.40, 64.15% complete), its phase 1 headquarters base (budget RMB 638,949,597.27, 30.35%) and a subsidiary's new-generation ICT product smart-factory project (budget RMB 999,384,774.44, 50.02%).
quarterly_data.figure: construction in progress RMB 573,184,168.51; new-generation ICT smart factory budget RMB 999,384,774.44 (50.02%)

quarterly_data.signal: Company plan for 2026 (annual report): it expects new information-infrastructure investment to keep rising and will embrace AI and intelligent-computing demand, while noting challenges from intensifying competition and supply-chain volatility. It will tighten profit-oriented performance management, focus resources on high-return products, secure supply, push new-product launches and build compute-tuning capability; at home it will balance intelligent-computing and non-intelligent-computing markets and pursue domestic-substitution opportunities, in internet and customised business it will strengthen R&D-to-supply-chain delivery to expand share, and overseas it will deepen channels and large global accounts to accelerate international growth.
